digest.component_or_area: review-bot voter and adapter; backfill reconciler safety net
propositions: A transient git fetch hang from the GitHub mirror (2-3s median, occasional 300s+ stalls) in clone_change_ref → resolve_ref → _fetch_origin times out after _GIT_TIMEOUT=300s, raising SnapshotFetchError.

adapter.code_review_decision blanket catches all exceptions and converts SnapshotFetchError (an infrastructure fault) to BLOCK/coverage-gap/review-error, indistinguishable from a genuine review finding.
voter.review_and_vote maps that BLOCK to llm_review_block_value=-1, POSTs the vote to Gerrit, and writes a dedup row, making the change permanently voted.

reconcile.py pre-filters out changes with existing LLM-Review votes via has_llm_review_vote, so the spurious -1 removes the change from backfill's safety net forever despite the -1 being due to a retryable infrastructure fault.

The infrastructure timeout (300s) always fires before the outer REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1200s), guaranteeing the vote-bearing error path is taken instead of the no-vote benign path already implemented at app.py and reconcile.py for hung reviews.

After fix: retryable infrastructure exceptions (SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) return ABSTAIN decision with no vote POST and no dedup row, leaving vote-less changes eligible for backfill re-review.
